keyFacts: SRT (SubRip) and WebVTT are the two most common subtitle formats on the internet.
The only timestamp difference is the millisecond separator: SRT uses a comma, WebVTT uses a dot.
WebVTT files must start with a WEBVTT header line; SRT files use sequential cue numbers instead.
The tool detects the format from your input, so you usually do not need to choose a direction manually.
Timing shifts move every cue forward or backward by the same amount in milliseconds.
All processing happens locally; subtitle text never leaves your browser.
